claims.text: The lab's db service is container donhang-db, published on host port 5432, seeded by db/seed.sql with 5 customers, 8 products and 12 orders.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: docker-compose.yml:57-73; db/seed.sql header comment

claims.text: Testcontainers (Testcontainers for .NET 4.15.0) starts a Docker container from test code and removes it when the container object is disposed; it needs a running Docker engine, not the Compose lab.
claims.source_hint: dotnet.testcontainers.org (overview, container lifecycle); verified by execution: docker events create/destroy during dotnet test (scratchpad it-a/evidence-tc.txt)

claims.text: PostgresFixture builds a PostgreSqlContainer with new PostgreSqlBuilder("postgres:17.6-alpine").WithDatabase("donhang").WithUsername("donhang").Build(); Build() only creates the description, StartAsync() starts the container, DisposeAsync() disposes it.
The test image postgres:17.6-alpine is the same image as the db service in docker-compose.yml at stage-2 (image: postgres:17.6-alpine).

Testcontainers' PostgreSQL module binds container port 5432 to a random free host port assigned when the container starts; GetConnectionString() returns host, mapped port, database, username and password.
claims.source_hint: dotnet.testcontainers.org modules/postgres; verified by execution: docker ps showed 0.0.0.0:54407->5432/tcp, docker events ports/5432/tcp=0.0.0.0:0

claims.text: The test container gets none of the lab's init SQL files and no named volume, so it starts with an empty database named donhang (WithDatabase); the postgres image runs docker-entrypoint-initdb.d files only on first start with an empty data directory.
claims.source_hint: PostgresFixture.cs:14-17; docker-compose.yml:67-71; postgres image docs (Initialization scripts); verified: InitialCreate applies

claims.text: InitializeAsync: container.StartAsync(), then MigrateAsync through CreateContext() (a DonHangDbContext on ConnectionString), applying every migration incl. InitialCreate; the schema includes FK_orders_customers_customer_id (AddOrderCustomerNavigation).
claims.source_hint: PostgresFixture.cs:26-38; Migrations/20260924092625_AddOrderCustomerNavigation.cs; EF Core docs: applying migrations at runtime

claims.text: EF Core's in-memory provider keeps data in memory, is not relational, runs no SQL and does not enforce foreign keys: SaveChanges accepts an order whose CustomerId names no customer, which PostgreSQL rejects (23503).

Lab db init scripts: schema.sql, seed.sql, migrations-baseline.sql (records InitialCreate as applied, as MigrationBaseline did until stage-1); db-data volume keeps rows. xUnit calls a class fixture's InitializeAsync/DisposeAsync once per test class.
DonHang.Tests.csproj at stage-2 references Testcontainers.PostgreSql (also Testcontainers.Redis, Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing); its comment says running the project now needs Docker, not the lab.
Tests that write to a shared lab database change data other users rely on, and their result depends on that data; a throwaway database avoids both.
`docker events --filter image=postgres:17.6-alpine --filter event=create --filter event=destroy` waits and prints one line per matching create or destroy event until stopped.
claims.source_hint: refs docker-docs data/cli/engine/docker_system_events.yaml (filters; same key repeated = OR, different keys = AND)

claims.text: In a stage-2 checkout with Docker running, `dotnet test DonHang.Tests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~EfOrderRepositoryTests"` passes 2 tests; docker events shows one create and one destroy line for a randomly named postgres:17.6-alpine container.
claims.source_hint: verified by execution on git archive stage-2, 2026-10-01 (scratchpad it-a/evidence-tc.txt)
